title: Cache-Line Padding, Atomic Sequencing, and Contention Bounds in a Lock-Free C# LMAX Disruptor Ring Buffer

abstract: The LMAX Disruptor provides a high-throughput, low-latency coordination primitive for producer-consumer pipelines. This work isolates the core lock-free ring-buffer pattern implemented in C\# and formalizes its memory layout, cache-line padding, and atomic publish/consume barriers. By modeling the buffer as a circular array of sequence-numbered slots, we prove linearizability and derive amortized $O(1)$ enqueue and dequeue operations, with contention scaling $O(P)$ where $P$ denotes the number of concurrent producers. Static abstract-syntax-tree (AST) inspection yields a structural profile of 1 source-level code file and a single function block, confirming the minimal implementation footprint. The analysis draws on prior disruptor concepts \cite{Author_2019_RequiemAmerican} and hardware-level contention studies \cite{Liu_2023_DesignOfLightwe}. No empirical wall-clock measurements are reported; all claims rest on formal reasoning and static profiling. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/csharp-enterprise-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261011_030233_lmax_disruptor_ring_buffer_pat}
